source.title: MLRG Deep Curvature
source.authors: Diego Granziol; Xingchen Wan; T. Garipov; D. Vetrov; Stephen J. Roberts

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no truncation or garbling materially affects the relevant result.
record.tranche_reason: It reports training-error outcomes for VGG-16 on CIFAR-100 under several optimizers, which bear on V1, but does not explicitly replicate the claim's random-initialization or label-corruption conditions.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports training-error curves for stochastic Lanczos Newton methods and Adam/SGD baselines. These are relevant results; no exact final training-error values are stated in the text. Other curvature and loss-landscape results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 measures VGG-16 training classification error on CIFAR-100 with SGD and Adam, matching V1's method and measure. The supplied text does not establish their final error rates or initialization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the package's purpose and the Figure 1 optimizer comparison. The paper's main conclusion concerns accessible curvature analysis and its mathematical foundations; it does not explicitly conclude that SGD or Adam reaches near-zero training error.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares stochastic Lanczos Newton methods with Adam and SGD on VGG-16/CIFAR-100; it does not specify random initialization or test the claim's conditions involving label corruption, width, or early stopping.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and learning rate are varied in the CIFAR-100 VGG-16 training-error plot.

fits_no_version.finding: Stochastic Lanczos Newton methods perform similarly across learning rates when damping is scaled with the learning rate; Adam converges more slowly per iteration and SGD follows an unstable trajectory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Damping-scaled stochastic Newton methods can improve convergence per iteration relative to the tested first-order optimizer settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The study measures Hessian spectra and local sensitivity to eigenvector perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curvature spectra and eigenvector perturbations characterize local training and testing landscapes.

record.problems: Training-error outcomes are shown in Figure 1 without text-stated numerical final values or uncertainty; the text characterizes optimizer comparisons but does not establish the initialization condition relevant to V1.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows extracted: Figure 1 is the only relevant training-error result, and its values are figure-only with no text description sufficient to determine whether each optimizer reaches near-zero error.

untested.parts: Corrupted or random labels, model-size comparisons, and effects of early stopping or regularization are not tested. Random initialization is unspecified. CIFAR-10 training accuracy is plotted, but its unperturbed value cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or comparison of student excess width.
No controlled comparison across depths or between plain and residual networks.
No comparison of initialization schemes, training speed under those schemes, or trainable depth.
No learning-rate comparison against the initial linearized stability limit or measurement of sharpness tracking the stability threshold.
No training-speed or learning-rate-tolerance comparison with and without batch normalization or Fixup.

missing.what: Unperturbed training classification accuracy for the SGD-trained VGG-16 models on CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10. Figures 10a and 12a contain potentially relevant baseline outcomes beyond Figure 1, but the supplied text preserves axis labels without readable curve values. Extract the zero-perturbation accuracy, rather than treating perturbed accuracies as independent training outcomes.
missing.locator: Sections 7 and 9; Figures 10a and 12a; epoch-300 checkpoints

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to correct. Figure 1's unreadable final outcomes are already declared in rows_left_out. No V1 verdict is justified by convergence-speed comparisons or an unstable trajectory alone: neither establishes whether final training classification error is near zero. The supplied text also gives inconsistent learning rates for the later SGD example: Section 7.1 states 1, while Appendix C specifies 0.05.

versions.untested_parts: Random initialization, CIFAR-10, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested. The figure gives no text-described final error values, so the plotted optimizer results cannot be extracted as determinate outcomes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
